Country.evidence_source: This study has several implications for prevention and intervention in both the Nepali context and low-income settings (outlined in Textbox 2) (Brent et al. 1996; Brent and Mann 2005; World Health Organization 2010).

Type.evidence_source: Although other larger PA case–control studies have been able to make populationlevel generalizations, our richer qualitative data on cultural understandings of suicide have unique potential to inform a host of prevention activities that quantitative studies cannot.

Area.evidence_source: A notable example is the rarity of decedents disclosing their thoughts of suicide to their family members. In fact, only 23% mentioned that their loved one had shared their suicide ideation. In many other low-income settings, suicide ideation disclosure is rare, often due to fear and stigma (Hagaman et al. 2013; Jordans et al. 2017).
